thread:
Carla - Support: Heads-up — AcmeMaps (private VPC) reporting intermittent inference requests that hang ~20-40s then either succeed or show TLS handshake errors ("tls: handshake timeout"). Started after infra hardened NACLs last week. Any ideas?

sre-acme: Yep, we rolled a NACL change Friday. Symptoms: client calls to /v1/generate sometimes return 524-like timeouts from our side; app logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts then eventual success. Happening ~5-10% of requests.

Tony - Eng Oncall: Okey. Two quick asks: 1) tcpdump from an affected inference host during a failing request (capture SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK) 2) NAT gateway/egress metrics (port allocations). Also paste the NACL rules for the subnet.

sre-acme: Attaching snippets. We don't want to paste full pcaps here but here's the tcpdump lines from the node during a failed attempt (remote model endpoint is 1.2.3.4:443):

```
20:12:01.123456 IP 10.0.5.21.54873 > 1.2.3.4.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
20:12:31.124000 IP 10.0.5.21.54873 > 1.2.3.4.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 (retransmission)
20:12:31.500900 IP 10.0.5.21.54874 > 1.2.3.4.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
20:12:31.501200 IP 1.2.3.4.443 > 54.239.10.101.54874: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 65535, length 0
20:12:31.501300 IP 1.2.3.4.443 > 54.239.10.101.54874: Flags [.], ack 1, win 65535, length 0
```

sre-acme: Notice that source ports change (54873 then 54874). Not sure why.

Tony - Eng Oncall: Interesting — that looks like the first SYN doesn't get a SYN-ACK, then client retries and a new source port is used. That pattern is consistent with asymmetric drop on the return path (NACL or firewall) or NAT port exhaustion/translation mapping weirdness. Can you paste the NACL rules for the subnet?

Marta - Eng Infra: Pulled NACL for subnet-id subnet-0a1b2c3d:

```
NetworkAclEntries:
- RuleNumber: 100, Protocol: -1, RuleAction: deny, Egress: false, CidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0, PortRange: 32768-61000
- RuleNumber: 110, Protocol: -1, RuleAction: allow, Egress: false, CidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
- RuleNumber: 120, Protocol: -1, RuleAction: allow, Egress: true, CidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
```

Marta - Eng Infra: Looks like someone added a deny inbound rule that matches before the allow and blocks the common ephemeral return port range. Because NACLs are stateless, you need both inbound and outbound allows for ephemeral ranges.

Carla - Support: That would explain why inbound SYN-ACKs aren't making it back to the instance for the original source port (54873) but later retries with a different ephemeral port occasionally make it through. Does AWS NAT gateway change source ports across retries?

Tony - Eng Oncall: NAT allocates ephemeral ports for SNAT; retries from the host that open a new socket may pick a new src port, and if the return path is blocked for the original translated port, it will drop. Also TLS sessions that cause connection re-establishment (e.g., client library timeouts) can trigger new ports and make the behavior intermittent.

Marta - Eng Infra: Quick repro suggestion: temporarily add an explicit allow rule for 32768-65535 inbound+outbound on that NACL at a higher priority (lower rule number) and retest. Also confirm no middlebox (WAF) is rewriting ports.

sre-acme: We applied a rule change: added allow inbound 32768-65535 ruleNumber 50 and allow outbound 32768-65535 ruleNumber 51. Ran a controlled test hitting the inference endpoint with a 100qps burst for 10s. Results: failure rate dropped from ~7% to 0.3%.

Marta - Eng Infra: Nice. Can you also share NAT gateway flow logs / CloudWatch NAT port allocation so we can see if port exhaustion was a contributing factor? If NAT was running low on ports we'd see many translations / reuse.

sre-acme: NAT metrics look normal, no port exhaustion. Root cause is the deny rule that was higher priority than the general allow — it was intended to lock down some legacy service but accidentally matched ephemeral ranges.

Carla - Support: Resolution path: 1) keep ephemeral allow entries on NACLs for the subnets hosting inference clients 2) audit for other NACLs with deny rules that could hit 32768-65535 3) add a short KB article in support about "NACL deny breaking TLS handshakes / intermittent connection failures" with triage commands.

Tony - Eng Oncall: Adding triage commands here for KB:
```
# tcpdump on instance (capture the 3-way handshake)
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 tcp and host 1.2.3.4 and port 443 -c 200
# check NACLs
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a1b2c3d
# NAT gateway translation logs (if enabled) / CloudWatch metrics
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/NATGateway --metric-name BytesOutToDestination --start-time ...
```

Carla - Support: Customer confirms stabilized after NACL change. We're going to roll a safer NACL change template into infra playbook and link it in the KB. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Incident note: ticket #INC-8842 resolved (root cause: NACL deny matched ephemeral port range causing asymmetric return-path drops leading to intermittent TLS handshake failures).
